items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: The interviewee does not speak in the provided context; the mention of Buddy DeFranco is made by the Interviewer as an example of musicians they have worked with.

ctx.x: I think it’s a good point too from the accompanist standpoint that they have to not only bring good music but a good personality to make things cohesive. Get that Kum-ba-ya you were talking about. Right?

I know when I worked with somebody like Al Cohn or Buddy DeFranco or Charlie Rouse, you know you find a way, they play a certain way. They play great. They played great, well Buddy is still living, all in their own ways, but you find a way of interacting with that and if you enjoy the way that you are interacting with it then you have fun working with this person. It doesn’t matter if he’s playing clarinet. You find Kum-ba-ya.
Is there any kind of, I’ll use the word inequality, in the marketing of jazz musicians these days according to their age? © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
